reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that the HEA (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 exhibits robust superconductivity up to 190.6 GPa, but it does not provide data on the bcc phase stability, the electronic density of states, or the pressure dependence of Tc for pure Nb/Ta, nor does it explicitly link the robustness to mixing entropy. Thus, the key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: High mixing entropy stabilizes the bcc phase against pressure-induced lattice distortions in the HEA.
The stable bcc lattice preserves an electronic structure favorable for Cooper pairing under pressure.
This structural stability leads to a Tc that is less degraded or even enhanced compared to pure bcc superconductors.
Pure bcc superconductors (Nb, Ta) show a different, likely decreasing, pressure dependence of Tc.
